question: Where do lexical/graph/semantic retrieval, index snapshot/freshness/invalidation/watchers/persistence/config fingerprints, query precision/coverage, large-repository scaling, and retrieval of cross-language implementation/test/command neighbors run through SDK/CLI consumers?

selectedFiles.reason: Real manager lifecycle: per-root/config singleton identity, bounded root registry, detached-holder mutation forwarding, monotonic epoch, background build/retry, readiness timeout, stale lexical query, asynchronous snapshot/vector pinning, CAS persistence handoff, snapshot identity, and failed embedding recovery.

Status and query failure surface consumed by the CLI: readiness/staleness/refreshing, parser versus budget coverage classification, semantic availability and skipped vectors, errors/timeouts, semantic file/path filtering, query-embedding fallback, and age/error refresh scheduling.

Persistence entrypoints: stat-first read cap, version/root and file-shape validation, accelerator rebuild, optional snapshot verification, ownership/CAS/newest-wins save, write/readback verification, tiered reduction, and chunk sidecar write relationship.

Published model-facing contract for graph/query modes, limits, extension/path scopes and traversal validation; result provenance, related files/snippets, canonical snapshot/status, structured build failures, and walker/parser coverage.

Actual query entrypoint and ranking: mode routing, path/file-type scopes, posting prefilter, lexical field/chunk scores, command intent, graph augmentation, tie ordering, neighbor/path output construction, explanation, and bounded snippets/results.

Graph consumers: top-seed neighborhood scoring, direct and gated shared-node expansion, second-hop fanout limits, relation provenance, shortest-path depth/queue bounds, seed resolution, directional reference/call results, and persisted adjacency coverage validation.

Large-index query accelerators: persisted postings/document frequencies/edge-index adjacency, yielding build variant, exact and substring candidate selection with union limits, per-query expansion scratch, capped frequency fallback, and chunk/name token coverage.

Semantic retrieval contract and implementation: credential-free provider/model/text-version fingerprint, bounded file embedding representation, exact-input vector reuse, batch/dimension checks and skipped-path diagnostics, query cosine ranking, and semantic/lexical score blending.

Index build/update orchestration rather than parser internals: walk versus precise-delta routing, stale revision rejection, stat/hash freshness gate, unchanged parse-result reuse, transient hash/content read retention, no-change diagnostic healing, degraded delta retention, deletions, graph/query-data regeneration, and coverage handoff.

Query-facing command metadata: native manifests across Rust/Go/Python/JVM/.NET/PHP/Swift/Ruby/CMake/Godot, package-script raw command concepts, task-runner concepts, CI extraction, and bounded concept payloads.

Large-repository eligibility and coverage boundary: nested ignore matchers, sensitive/operational/binary/oversized filtering, no-follow traversal checks, fair-share prefix buckets, round-robin file cap, and skipped-file/prefix accounting.

Actual CLI query_index client-tool override: live indexing config, disabled output, configured embedder, 2-second readiness wait, queryBlended invocation, canonical result/status/snapshot conversion, semantic notice, related-file propagation, and mutation epoch publication.

Real run consumer wiring: watcher construction, paths-only initial project context, successful SDK create/update/delete/move deltas with workspace revision, conservative onFilesChanged invalidation for unknown mutation surfaces, and best-effort callback failures.

External-edit invalidation lifecycle: platform branch, classification of cache/file/delete/directory events, root cap and cleanup, debounced precise versus pathless invalidation, Linux worker pool callbacks, dynamic directory add/remove, and recursive/worker failure fallback.

Real SDK client-tool execution boundary: custom-handler validation/cancellation, client-tool recognition, override resolution and execution, and entry into default dispatch; inspect the final unsupported-tool/error-envelope branch in the secondary SDK range.

Existing behavioral evidence for labeled stale snapshots during refresh, refreshed command snippets, age-driven background refresh, precise delta revision/snapshot/hash outputs, and structured nonretryable cache-ownership failure.

Existing adversarial semantic evidence: snapshot replacement during query embedding, changed provider cacheKey rewiring, and prior-vector availability after a failing refresh embedder. Read the actual test mechanics before assigning assurance.

Versioned quality gates against the actual repository index plus evaluator metric contract: Recall@K/MRR/nDCG/noise, corpus/file expectations, injected timing behavior, and explicit lexical retrieval path.

scopeBoundaries: Pair07 owns code-map parser/language/AST/LSP/import resolver and SCIP extraction/runner mechanics. This shard selects their returned metadata, graph/query consumption, and persistence seams only.
Pair06 owns mutation authority, exact-byte edit correctness, and broker/transaction durability; this shard traces emitted mutations into retrieval freshness.
